learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how nutritional needs change throughout the human lifespan and how proper diet maintains health and well-being at every age!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Breast milk is the perfect food for the first 6 months as it provides all nutrients and builds immunity. After 6 months, 'weaning' starts by introducing soft, mashed solid foods.
School-going children need energy-dense and protein-rich foods for growth and physical activity. Breakfast is critical to maintain concentration in school.
Adults need a balanced diet to maintain weight and prevent lifestyle diseases. Pregnant and lactating women have special requirements, needing extra calories, iron, and folic acid.
The elderly have a slower metabolism and need fewer calories, but they still need high vitamins and minerals. Their food should be easy to chew and digest.
Well-being is a holistic concept. It means being physically fit, mentally peaceful, emotionally stable, and socially connected. Good nutrition is the foundation of this holistic health.

fun_activity.title: 🥣 The Weaning Menu
fun_activity.instructions: Design a 'First Food' menu for a 7-month-old baby. Remember, they don't have teeth and their stomach is tiny! (Hint: Mashed banana, watery dal, or boiled mashed potato).

exam_tips: 📌 Know the definition of 'Weaning' and why it starts at 6 months.
📌 Highlight that elderly people need fewer calories but higher fiber and calcium.
📌 Be ready to explain the specific nutritional needs of a pregnant woman (focus on Iron and Folic acid).
quick_recap: ⭐ Nutritional requirements change based on age, gender, and physical activity.
⭐ Breast milk provides natural antibodies to protect infants from infections.
⭐ Malnutrition includes both undernutrition (deficiency) and overnutrition (obesity).
